metadata.title: The Fall and the Promise of the Seeds
metadata.summary: Adam and Eve are expelled from Paradise. As Adam nears death, he sends his son Seth to the gates of Eden to ask for the Oil of Mercy. Instead, Seth is given three seeds from the Tree of Knowledge to place in Adam's mouth.
metadata.setting: The Gates of Paradise / The Toilsome Earth

content.cornish: An Tas a dhewl Adam hag Eva yn-mes a Baradhys.
content.narrative: The Father casts Adam and Eve out of Paradise.
content.marginalia: This is the 'Anken' (Sorrow) that begins the human journey.

content.cornish: A Arluth, tru! My yw dregis; / Anken bras yw dhybm degis.
content.narrative: O Lord, alas! I am rejected; / Great sorrow is brought to me.

prefiguration.description: Adam's despair here is mirrored by his joy when Christ leads him back into Paradise in Act IV.

content.cornish: Yn dhowr ha hwys ty a dheber / dhy'th vara, kyn fylly'th her.
content.narrative: In water and sweat thou shalt eat / thy bread, though thy strength fail.

content.cornish: Adam ow kallegy Seth dhe dhorow Paradhys.
content.narrative: Adam, old and dying, calls Seth to the doors of Paradise.
content.notes: The transition from the 'Exile' to the 'Promise of the Wood'.

content.cornish: Tas, my a dhe dhe'n porthow; / Oyl a versy yw ow dhow.
content.narrative: Father, I go to the gates; / The Oil of Mercy is my desire.

content.cornish: An El a rhydh tri hasen dhe Seth rag y das.
content.narrative: The Angel gives three seeds to Seth for his father.
content.marginalia: The Cedar, Cypress, and Pine. These are the physical origin of the Rood.

prefiguration.description: These three seeds will grow into the one tree used for the Cross, reuniting the wood of the Fall with the wood of Salvation.
